title: Grade 10 English — Subject-Verb Agreement & Prepositions
description: Subject-Verb Agreement and Prepositions and Conjunctions practice questions
subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct form: Neither he nor his friends ___ coming to the party.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearest subject. 'his friends' (plural) is closer to the verb, so 'are' is correct.

questions.question: 'The jury ___ reached its verdict.' Choose the correct verb.
questions.explanation: Collective nouns (jury, committee, team) take singular verbs when acting as a unit. 'The jury has' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: Five hundred rupees ___ a lot of money for a child.
questions.explanation: When an amount of money, weight, or time is treated as a single entity, it takes a singular verb. 'Five hundred rupees is' (the sum as a whole).

questions.question: 'Each of the students ___ submitted the assignment.' Choose the correct verb.
questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns like 'each', 'every', 'either', 'neither' take singular verbs. 'Each has' is correct.

questions.question: Subject-verb agreement rule: when the subject is compound (A and B), the verb is usually:
questions.explanation: When two subjects are joined by 'and', the compound subject is plural and takes a plural verb. Example: 'Ram and Shyam are friends.'

questions.question: 'The news ___ good.' Which is correct?
questions.explanation: Some nouns ending in -s are singular: news, mathematics, physics, economics. 'The news is' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: She has been waiting ___ two hours.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration (two hours, three days, a week). 'Since' is used with a point in time (since morning, since 2020).

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The cat is sitting ___ the table.
questions.explanation: 'On' indicates position on a surface. 'In' = inside an enclosed space. 'At' = at a specific point. 'The cat is on the table' means sitting on top of it.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: She arrived ___ Monday morning.
questions.explanation: Time prepositions: 'at' for specific times (at 8 o'clock), 'on' for days and dates (on Monday, on 14th July), 'in' for months/years/seasons (in January, in 2024).

questions.question: Choose the conjunction: She studied hard ___ she wanted to pass.
questions.explanation: 'Because' introduces a reason. 'She studied hard because she wanted to pass' — cause-effect relationship. 'Although' shows contrast.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: He tried hard ___ he failed.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' (coordinating conjunction) shows contrast or unexpected result: 'He tried hard yet he failed.' Similar to 'but'.

questions.question: The phrase 'in spite of' is followed by:
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' and 'despite' are prepositions — they must be followed by a noun, pronoun, or gerund (V-ing noun). Example: 'In spite of the rain, they played.'

questions.question: '___ all his efforts, he did not succeed.' Choose the correct phrase.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' (preposition) + noun phrase expresses contrast. 'Despite' works similarly. 'Although' is used before a clause (subject + verb).

questions.question: A correlative conjunction works in pairs. Which is a correct pair?
questions.explanation: Correlative conjunctions come in pairs: either...or, neither...nor, both...and, not only...but also, whether...or. 'Either...or' is the correct pair.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The book was written ___ Charles Dickens.
questions.explanation: 'By' is used in passive constructions to indicate the agent (the doer). 'Written by Charles Dickens' identifies the author.
